scope: Bounded candidate sources on reported past-life memories, reincarnation-type case methods, and psychological or cultural effects of karma belief
relationship_to_pr_329: Separate companion crawl only. It supplies a reincarnation and karma comparison lane without changing, depending on, or expanding PR #329's canonical effect.
scope_boundaries: A scientifically unusual or well-documented case may justify closer study without establishing reincarnation, postmortem survival, or a transfer mechanism.
Studies of karma belief measure human cognition, attribution, honesty, generosity, punishment, or social judgment; they do not test metaphysical karmic causation.
Spontaneous childhood reports are kept distinct from hypnotic regression, recovered-memory practices, mediumship, dreams, and adult retrospective narratives.
Karma and rebirth have non-identical meanings across Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, Sikh, and other traditions; this crawl does not define a universal doctrine.
Archive inclusion is not endorsement, falsification, or canonical acceptance.
retrieval_limits: Bibliographic records, abstracts, official repositories, and open full-text records were reviewed; not every source received a line-by-line full-text claim audit.
No case was independently reinvestigated and no original interview, translation, family record, death record, medical record, or matching procedure was revalidated.

Case-series publication, pre-identification notes, or apparent correspondence can reduce particular retrospective concerns but cannot by themselves exclude leakage, selective reporting, coincidence, translation effects, fraud, or analytical flexibility.
Psychological counter-sources on memory and suggestibility identify general risks and do not adjudicate any individual reincarnation-type case.
No survival mechanism, karmic law, rebirth process, personal identity continuity, or nonlocal information channel is authenticated.

requirements: Do not collapse distinct Indian religious and philosophical traditions into a single Westernized reward-punishment model.
Separate participant belief measures from the doctrines, practices, languages, and communities from which karma and rebirth concepts arise.
Seek cultural and tradition-specific review before public interpretation.
Avoid caste, poverty, disability, bereavement, or victim-blaming implications that treat suffering as deserved.

sources.title: Personhood in Classical Indian Philosophy
sources.claim_boundary: Provides conceptual provenance and contrasts among philosophical accounts; it is not empirical evidence for karma or rebirth.

sources.title: The Content and Correlates of Belief in Karma Across Cultures
sources.claim_boundary: Supports measurement of explicit karma beliefs and their correlates across sampled populations; correlations do not establish metaphysical karma or causal effects of belief.

sources.publisher: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics
sources.title: Karma and honest behavior: An experimental study
sources.claim_boundary: Tests whether a karma intervention affects reported or observed honesty under the study design; it does not test supernatural moral causation.

sources.title: How Karma Harms and Helps Generosity Toward Those in Need
sources.claim_boundary: Supports bounded claims about how thinking about karma can relate to both helping and blame or inequality judgments in sampled settings; it does not validate karmic causation or generalize to all traditions.

sources.title: Academic studies on claimed past-life memories: A scoping review
sources.claim_boundary: Establishes the existence, distribution, and methodological profile of a published observational literature; it does not establish reincarnation or survival.

sources.title: Children Who Claim to Remember Previous Lives: Cases with Written Records Made before the Previous Personality Was Identified
sources.claim_boundary: Pre-identification written records address one form of post-contact memory inflation; the cases remain observational and do not exclude all normal information pathways, selection effects, coincidence, or record-quality problems.

sources.title: Do attitudes of families concerned influence features of children who claim to remember previous lives?
sources.claim_boundary: Examines whether family attitudes are associated with reported case features; association does not fully explain the reports and does not validate reincarnation.

sources.title: Suggestibility of the child witness: A historical review and synthesis
sources.claim_boundary: Supplies general child-memory and interview-method risks relevant to case assessment; it is not a case-specific refutation and should not be used to dismiss a report without examining its actual documentation.

sources.title: Impact of children's purported past-life memories: a follow-up investigation of American cases
sources.claim_boundary: Supports bounded observations about later characteristics and reported impact among a followed case sample; it does not verify the historical content of childhood reports or demonstrate survival.

candidate_links.note: Pre-identification documentation is a higher-priority outlier feature for prospective methodological study, not a truth label.
Assess timing and specificity of records together with family expectations, interview structure, leakage pathways, base rates, and selective reporting.
Research value includes psychosocial impact and family response even if the metaphysical hypothesis remains unresolved.
Treat belief as a psychological and cultural variable with potentially prosocial and harmful attribution effects; do not infer a cosmic mechanism.
Empirical scales are operationalizations, not substitutes for tradition-specific accounts of karma, personhood, and rebirth.

outlier_priority_rules: Prioritize statements recorded before any candidate previous person or family is identified.
Preserve the complete original statement set, including vague, wrong, unmatched, and later-modified items.
Use preregistered matching rules, blinded independent raters, decoy candidates, base-rate estimates, and correction for multiple comparisons.
Document every direct and indirect information pathway, interpreter role, media exposure, geographic link, and contact timeline.
Separate observation, witness recollection, investigator inference, record verification, and metaphysical interpretation.
Seek independent replication and adversarial audit before any evidential promotion.
Use trauma-informed, non-leading interviews and child safeguarding; research interest never overrides participant welfare or privacy.

excluded_or_deferred.reason: High suggestibility and source-monitoring risk; requires a separate memory-method review before inclusion.
May be retained later as attributed lived experience, but is not part of this scientific-method companion crawl.

excluded_or_deferred.category: individual child case identities and media
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Privacy, safeguarding, consent, and rights review required.
Outside the empirical scope and prohibited by the no-truth-inference boundary.

priorities.use: Build a prospective case-quality rubric for claimed past-life memories.
priorities.deliverable: Methods-and-countermethods matrix with leakage, matching, memory, cultural, privacy, and safeguarding fields.

priorities.use: Track later psychosocial outcomes separately from claim verification.
priorities.deliverable: Child-and-family impact review with no metaphysical inference.

priorities.use: Map empirical karma-belief constructs and their mixed behavioral effects.
priorities.deliverable: Belief-behavior evidence table separating prosocial effects, blame, system justification, correlation, and experiment.

priorities.use: Compare person, memory, pattern, relationship, process, and culturally situated continuity models.
priorities.deliverable: Tradition-aware comparison layer; no universal karma definition and no survival promotion.

governance_requirements: No canonical edge, public route, public synthesis, or truth inference is created by this record.
Keep Established Evidence, Interpretation, Lived Experience/Testimony, Hypothesis, and Speculation distinct.
Preserve nulls, mismatches, counter-sources, uncertainty, source independence, and evidence lineage.
Require human full-text, cultural, rights, privacy, and safeguarding review before canonical or public integration.

next_gate: Fresh exact-head review of provenance, claim labels, limitations, counter-methods, cultural handling, child privacy, rights, and roadmap mapping; any later canonical or public use requires a separate human-approved integration decision.
